column5: reason
CRED free-living coral is mostly Fungiidae (mushroom) plus a few free-living non-fungiids; approximate is the right grade
mobile fauna are echinoderms, molluscs, crustaceans, fish; OTHER_FAUNA is the residual-animal bucket outside Cnidaria and Porifera
T3 code for the same mobile-fauna concept as MF

the vocab also has separate Substrate and Water classes, so Background may hold non-seagrass biota (algae); ABIOTIC would then assert "non-living" wrongly. Needs the dataset paper's class definition; UNKNOWN or unmappable are the fallbacks
VME "coral" includes stylasterid hydrocorals (Hydrozoa); Anthozoa invented a class for them. Now Cnidaria, coarsened (smallest accepted clade)
coral spans Anthozoa and hydrozoan fire corals; now Cnidaria, coarsened
same as ruod: now Cnidaria, coarsened
brown algae are Chromista, so no single clade short of Biota; Plantae is the best overlap and correctly marked approximate
UIIS10K "plants" = seagrass plus macroalgae; same reasoning as aquatic plants
empty shells are almost all bivalve and gastropod; "dead remains" cannot be expressed on rs-taxa-v1 (taxon axis only), which the note records
TrashCan "plant" = marine vegetation including algae; same reasoning as aquatic plants
natural wood, not litter; NT_DEBRIS is the only non-taxon bucket that fits and the note says so
uncolonised rock or sand; ABIOTIC is its strict parent
scleractinians outside the source's genus list; HC is a strict ancestor
any biological material; Biota (AphiaID 1) is the only exact-or-broader anchor
morphospecies; the family is the strict ancestor
morphospecies; the order is the strict ancestor
a cf. identification is not a species claim; genus is the honest level
two sea-pen genera in different families; the order is their smallest shared accepted clade in the snapshot

fish is paraphyletic and WoRMS Pisces is unaccepted; Vertebrata is the smallest accepted clade holding all fish, note lists includes: [Actinopterygii, Elasmobranchii, Holocephali, Myxini, Petromyzonti]

column5: CoralNet 79 = Millepora; MIL (Millepora 205902) existed, the WP-7b note 'no genus node yet' was false. Was CN_HYDROZOA coarsened
CoralNet 403 = Halimeda; HA (Halimeda 143820) existed. Was SW (macroalgae) coarsened with a false 'no genus node' note
CoralNet 342 = sea urchins; URCH (Echinoidea 123082) existed. Was OTHER_FAUNA coarsened
CoralNet 3208 = Anemone; ANEM (Actiniaria 1360) existed. Was CNIDARIA coarsened
CoralNet 4095 = Chlorophyta, not generic algae: GA was read as 'green/generic algae' from the code alone. Was ALGAE coarsened
CoralNet 1175 XENIIDAE 'Family Xeniidae'; WoRMS 125271 accepted, lineage Octocorallia > Malacalcyonacea. 21% of points
CoralNet 102 Sponge 'group label for all types of sponges' = Porifera
CoralNet 3438 Hard Substrate 'can be pavement, dead coral, turf algae'; spans abiotic, transition and algae, so a root non_taxon node, not RK (rock/pavement only)
CoralNet 2040 Rhytisma; the page's functional group says Soft Substrate, but the name is the octocoral genus (WoRMS 267812, Lemnaliidae, Animalia) used by the Red Sea sources that share the label
CoralNet 1012 'Aglaophenia spp., ostrich-plume hydroid'; WoRMS 116999 accepted (Aglaopheniidae)
CoralNet 4081 Rhodophyta; WoRMS 852 accepted. Parent ALGAE, as for the other phylum nodes
CoralNet 642 'Algae (filamentous): uniseriate, simple, AKA turf'; the label's own definition equates it with turf
CoralNet 1637 'Framer in the photograph' = quadrat frame; TWS is the survey-equipment node and carries the 'quadrat' alias
CoralNet 80 'Cnidaria: Octocorallia' = SC (Octocorallia 1341)
CoralNet 105 'Dead skeletons - not colonized' = DC (dead coral)
CoralNet 1974 Porites (massive): taxon + morphology attribute (CATAMI style); coarsened is conservative but not wrong
PIFSC ACTA = Acropora, tabulate; genus + form attribute
POCS = Pocillopora sp.
DISP = Diploastrea sp.
rounded-leaf morphotype = Halophila ovalis group; genus is a strict ancestor

concept is the WoRMS genus name; node name identical
subgenus form matches the WoRMS record verbatim

WoRMS treats melanura as a spelling variant of accepted Oblada melanurus; the same species, so exact
PLC Turf = turf algae
RUOD 'echinus' is its sea-urchin class (not the genus Echinus); Echinoidea
material kept only in the source label; debris is the strict parent
processed-wood litter (natural wood is trash_branch, approximate); debris is the strict parent

column5: v13i presence tag: 379/384 images also carry Healthy/Bleached, so it is not an image class; UNKNOWN asserts no taxon and nothing on condition
current CoralNet group; HS (hard substrate, cover unspecified) is the node for exactly that roll-up; members seen here (1340 CCA on hard substrate, 7011 COTS predation) are all finer
group is mostly sand/silt/mud but curators file some biota in it (reefolution Rhy), so the ABIOTIC roll-up can be wrong: approximate, never coarsened
overrides NOAA BR "NO RULE"; HC + CB is exactly what the label says; coarsened under-claims but is safe
rs-benthic-v1 has no columnar form node (CB/CE/CF/CM/CS/CMR/CD/CT/CMD), so only the taxon is kept; nothing invented
Tridacninae are Bivalvia; CLAM (Bivalvia, alias tridacna) is a strict ancestor
may be a cnidarian (hydroid, anemone) or OTHER_FAUNA; their lowest common ancestor is BIOTIC, so nothing finer is true
Antipatharia (Hexacorallia); no Anthozoa or antipatharian node exists, CNIDARIA is the coarsest true node
a COTS feeding scar is recently dead coral; DC keeps the state and loses only the cause
Heliopora (blue coral) is an octocoral; SC_HELIOPORA carries AphiaID 206210 Heliopora; the label is genus-level
CCA is the taxon; "on hard substrate" is the CRED substrate qualifier, not a different organism; 91,773 NOAA points

target right, fidelity arguable: TWS is a compound bucket (tape/wand/shadow), so wand is strictly finer (coarsened). All 5 TWS edges are exact by one codegen rule (taxonomy_codegen.py:147-150); change the rule, not one edge
hydroids are colonial hydrozoan polyps; Hydrozoa is the strict parent (MIL is its own node and is not asserted)
both genera are Dictyotaceae; the family is the lowest node containing both
genus and growth form both have nodes; nothing lost
sand = SD; 9,709 Reefolution points

was exact. Binary CORAL/CORAL_BL split assessed no other condition, so the class asserts only "not bleached"; same rule as Roboflow Healthy and RS non_bleached (manager decision 2; test_binary_not_bleached_labels_share_one_rule)
was HC. Class-agnostic masks over hard and soft coral; no Anthozoa node, so the lowest node holding HC and SC is CNIDARIA (manager decision 1; MAJOR, 2.0.0)

target right. By the Fidelity definition (exact = same meaning) this is exact; the header even says "four of five labels are EXACT". Coarsened only because growth form was not recorded, which is another axis. Kept: not in the WP-7d decisions
same as Hard Coral: SC (Octocorallia) is what the Caribbean field label means; exact vs coarsened hinges on the unrecorded form axis. Kept, question open
